newsitem.title: GERMANY: German advertising sales growth slowing - study.
newsitem.headline: German advertising sales growth slowing - study.

text.p: The growth of the German advertising market is slowing down, media marketing company IP Deutschland said on Tuesday.

IP Deutschland predicted net spending for media, cinema and billboard advertising would increase by only 1.9 percent to 32.8 billion marks, a rate even below the expected 2.5 percent expansion of the German economy for 1997.

"The lack of a big jump in private consumption is mirrored in advertising expenditures," said IP Deutschland spokeswoman Susanne Baldauf said. "They seem to fail to be matching the rate of growth of previous years."
Advertising turnover increased 3.4 percent in 1996 from the previous year's sales.

The marketing company's parent company Havas released a study in Paris on Tuesday in which it estimated a 4.9 percent boost in advertising spending in Europe for the current year over 1996 to 233 billion marks.

The study called Germany the largest national advertising market by far, with a steady 29.3 percent of total spending going toward ads, but the strongest growth came in Britain with a 7.3 percent rise in spending.
